Builds on: open one to see the idea this puzzle uses.

  • Puzzle 1: One token at a time

    A language model reads and writes tokens: words, pieces of words, characters. It produces an answer by next-token prediction: given all the text so far, pick one next token, append it, and run again, until it stops. Limits, latency and price are all counted in tokens, and longer answers take longer because each token is one more step.

Starting from zero? The blocks under this puzzle are 2 puzzles: 0 → 1. Know them already? Start here.

The problem

You know the model continues text and counts in tokens. But what does the request look like, in code you could write with OkHttp? And what comes back besides the answer?

See it

Save this diagram as a GIF

The building block

A call to Anthropic's Messages API is one HTTP POST with a JSON body (shown slightly simplified):

{
  "model": "MODEL_NAME",
  "max_tokens": 300,
  "messages": [
    { "role": "user", "content": "Summarise this review: …" }
  ]
}
  • model: which model to use, a name from the provider's docs.
  • max_tokens: the most tokens the answer may have.
  • messages: the conversation as a list of turns, each marked user (your side) or assistant (the model's earlier answers). Puzzle 4 shows why that list matters.

The response, also JSON:

{
  "content": [ { "type": "text", "text": "Short battery life, great screen." } ],
  "stop_reason": "end_turn",
  "usage": { "input_tokens": 312, "output_tokens": 9 }
}

Three things to read every time:

  • the text in content;
  • stop_reason: end_turn means the model finished; max_tokens means it was cut off at your limit, mid-sentence;
  • usage: the input and output tokens of this call. That's the bill: providers charge per token, and output tokens cost several times more than input ones. Output is also what takes time, one token per step (puzzle 1).

The analogy

A telegram service that charges per word, with a higher rate for the reply. You state the maximum reply length up front, and if the reply hits it, it stops, mid-sentence.

Sources
  • Anthropic: Messages API examples (a response contains content, stop_reason such as "end_turn" or "max_tokens", and "usage": { "input_tokens": …, "output_tokens": … }; requests send model, max_tokens and messages with roles)
  • Anthropic: Pricing (input and output tokens are priced separately, output higher)

What you now know

A call to a model is one HTTP POST: a model name, max_tokens (the most it may write), and messages, a list of turns each marked user or assistant. The response holds the continuation, a stop_reason (end_turn when it finished, max_tokens when it was cut off), and usage: the input and output tokens you pay for. Output tokens cost more than input ones, and each one takes time to generate.
